## POSTSEPTAL CELLULITIS (ORBITAL CELLULITIS)
Postseptal cellulitis (orbital cellulitis) is often preceded by sinusitis and
requires immediate consultation with otolaryngology and ophthalmology. Urgent
surgical drainage may be necessary. The most common pathogenic organisms in
adults are streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus
aureus. Broad-spectrum empirical antimicrobials should be used until a pathogen
can be identified from the drainage fluid.
## Duration of treatment
Orbital cellulitis should be treated until all signs of infection have resolved.
Uncomplicated orbital cellulitis should be treated for minimum of 2 weeks and
complicated orbital cellulitis (severe ethmoid sinusitis and bony destruction of
sinus) should be treated for at least 4 weeks.
## Empiric treatment
Preferred:
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
Alternative:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h ($) [DI]
<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]
## Step-down treatment after initial intravenous therapy. Base selection on cultur
## results. Adjust duration based on criteria above.
Preferred:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID ($) [R] < AND >
trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 7 days
Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h ($) [R] < AND > trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO
q12h ($) [R,DI] for 7 days
